newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firms after hefty EU export bids.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firms after hefty EU export bids.

text.p: French wheat prices rose on Thursday as sellers took to the sidelines after exporters bid via France to export over 600,000 tonnes of soft wheat at this week's European Union grain auction.
"The large export bids made sellers cautious," one dealer said.
In France exporters bid to ship 658,000 tonnes of European Union wheat at rebates ranging from 17.69 to 21.24 Ecus per tonne.
February wheat into Rouen was paid at 855 francs per tonne for public silo, up five francs on Wednesday.
Buyers paid 852.50 francs per tonne for March wheat into Rouen and bid 847.50 francs per tonne for April, both up 2.50 francs on the previous day.
Several exporters said they expected the European Union to grant a wheat export refund of some 18.50 Ecus per tonne, covering the export of up to 244,000 tonnes in France.
They hoped the European Commission would continue to back wheat exports this week, having raised the refund on wheat by four Ecus to 18.99 Ecus per tonne last week.
"The Commission is in a better frame of mind and the market hopes it will confirm it is willing to export," one dealer said.
Exporters also said the large tonnage sought this week was linked to the recent sale of 500,000 tonnes of French wheat to Egypt.
Rouen barley for February was steady at 850-855 francs per tonne although exporters bid in France to ship 165,000 tonnes of EU barley at the auction.

Bordeaux maize for February-March delivery was steady at 840 francs per tonne as operators awaited the outcome of a second round of special tenders for the preferential import of non-EU maize and sorghum to Spain and Portugal.
French grain prices exclude domestic carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne, which must be added to every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question.
May fob barge Matif wheat futures were bid at 882 francs per tonne and offered at 890 but there was no trade.
